newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady ahead of U.S. holiday.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady ahead of U.S. holiday.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures steadied into the close as late short covering ahead of the long weekend holiday in the U.S. firmed NYMEX crude and expiring September heating oil contracts, traders said.
October Brent crude futures last traded three cents a barrel higher at $20.78 after rallying to a new contract high of $21 a barrel at this morning's opening.
Its $21 high was the strongest for a spot contract since April 15 but traders said there was little volume to the rise.
"The last five to 10 cents of this morning's rally was on very thin volume," one trader said.
Support at $20.70 held but trade was cautious due to uncertainty as to how NYMEX would react ahead of its three-day Labor Day weekend and the Sept product futures expiries.
Gas oil futures ended near session lows on profit taking and book squaring ahead of the U.S. Labor Day holiday weekend.
"Technicals are still showing the market overbought and NYMEX heat weakened over the afternoon so people took profits and squared out ahead of the weekend," a broker said.
After charging to 4-1/2 month highs on Thursday, selling into the close pegged September gas oil futures back to last trade at $196.75 a tonne, unchanged from Thursday's settlement.
Some traders expect gas oil futures could further extend gains next week despite the market's overbought state.
"There are market rumours that because of the change in spec to 0.05 diesel in October, (a trading company) may try and squeeze the 0.2 market," a broker said.

Some traders thought both Brent and gas oil futures may weaken first though on Monday when the NYMEX is closed and the products will not be able to prop up the London market, as the case has been this week.
